title: From Austerity to Deflationary Abundance: Measuring Real Flourishing Beyond GDP
tagline: Retiring 1934 GDP blindness for Real Household Flourishing Telemetry as clean energy and robotics collapse the cost of thriving by 70%.
cynicBelief: Even if AI, robotics, and solar energy make goods radically cheaper, falling prices will trigger a 1930s debt-deflation crash, shrink tax revenues, bankrupt homeowners with fixed mortgages, and trap governments in permanent austerity.
breakthroughCounter: Twentieth-century GDP (P × Q) missed trillions in consumer surplus when Wikipedia replaced $1,500 encyclopedias and solar fell 99.6%. By combining Stanford's GDP-B consumer-surplus accounting, New Zealand's Well-Being Budget, and a Dual-Regime Monetary Rule that locks nominal household cash inflows at +4%/yr while letting clean tech collapse essential living costs 60–80%, families stay 100% mortgage-solvent while gaining massive discretionary freedom.
socialNormShift: Upgrading national and municipal scoreboards from raw corporate billing volume (1934 GDP) to the Thriving Basket Workweek—celebrating technological price drops as human time-wealth liberation.

humanStory.snippet: While Elena's nominal family cash inflow grew steadily to $116,500—making her fixed $2,100 legacy mortgage effortless—her annual bill for power, food, housing, and preventative care plunged 72% to $15,400, cutting her household's survival workweek from 38.4 hours down to 14.2 hours.

quote.text: GDP measures market transactions, not human well-being—when technology makes vital goods nearly free, our true prosperity soars even if traditional price gauges miss the miracle.

cynicBelief: Sidewalk tent encampments, open-air fentanyl tragedy, and transit psychosis are permanent in modern cities—we already spend billions and nothing works except endless sweeps or decay.
breakthroughCounter: Cities burn $75,000/yr per unhoused neighbor on futile ER/jail sweeps! Meanwhile, Finland's Y-Foundation cut chronic homelessness >80% (virtually zero street sleeping in Helsinki, saving €15k/person/yr), Houston's unified Way Home dashboard housed 30,000+ people (-63% unsheltered), and Austin's Community First! Village hit 86% retention across sunlit micro-homes and artisan barns.
socialNormShift: Replacing chaotic gym-mat cots and 5-year $750k condo bottlenecks with 30-day state-preempted $22k solar micro-cottages, one outcome-paid dashboard, and Compassionate Tri-Track care (rent bridge, GLP-1/LIFU addiction villages, and muscarinic garden villas).

humanStory.protagonist: Marcus Bell, 52-Year-Old Village Ceramist & Former Overpass Resident
humanStory.location: Seattle Evergreen Village & Austin Community First! Model
humanStory.snippet: After years of $78,000/yr ER-to-asphalt cycling, a peer navigator matched Marcus in 20 minutes via a Houston-style live tablet into a lockable cedar cottage, quieted his fentanyl cravings biologically with GLP-1 therapy, and welcomed him into the pottery barn—where he now earns $1,400/month, pays $380 rent proudly, and hosts Tuesday porch pancakes.

quote.text: The catastrophic loss of family is the primary driver of homelessness—housing alone will never solve homelessness, but community will.
quote.author: Alan Graham
quote.role: Founder & CEO, Mobile Loaves & Fishes / Community First! Village
